title: Determination of the Incidence of Anteroinferior Shoulder Dislocation During Membership in the German National Canoe Slalom Squad Between 2000 and 2025.
summary:
Background: In canoe slalom, falls and awkward movements can lead to shoulder injuries. One possible injury is a shoulder dislocation, in which the humeral head slips out of its normal position in the shoulder socket. The frequency of this injury among members of the German National Canoe Slalom Squad has not yet been sufficiently investigated.

Research question: The aim of this study is to determine how often shoulder dislocations occurred among current and former members of the German National Canoe Slalom Squad between 2000 and 2025. The study will also investigate how often the injury recurs, how often affected athletes subsequently return to training and competition, and which movements or body positions may play a role in shoulder dislocations.

Methods: Current and former members of the German national canoe slalom squad will be invited to complete a questionnaire once. The questionnaire will collect information on previous shoulder dislocations, recurrent injuries, and return to sport, among other aspects. In addition, existing video footage provided by the German Canoe Federation will be analysed to investigate movements and body positions associated with shoulder dislocations in greater detail. Participation in the study is voluntary.

interventions.name: Current and former athletes who were members of the German national canoe slalom squad between 2000 and 2025. A one-time retrospective assessment using a digital or postal questionnaire to collect data on anteroinferior shoulder dislocations sustained during squad membership, recurrent dislocations,

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult current and former canoe slalom athletes who were members of the German national canoe slalom squad between 2000 and 2025.
Exclusion criteria:
Athletes will be excluded if their first shoulder dislocation occurred prior to joining the national squad, if they are under 18 years of age at the time of data collection, or if they have not provided informed consent to participate in the study.
